ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $CD$ is the altitude on the hypotenuse $AB$. If $AD=3$ and $BD=2$, what is the length of $CD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle ACD+\angle BCD=90^\circ$.\\
Since $CD$ is the altitude from the hypotenuse $AB$,\\
it follows that $\angle ADC=\angle CDB=90^\circ$, $\angle ACD+\angle CAD=90^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle CAD=\angle BCD$,\\
therefore $\triangle CAD\sim \triangle BCD$,\\
therefore $\frac{AD}{CD}=\frac{CD}{BD}$,\\
therefore $CD^2=3\times 2=6$,\\
therefore $CD=\sqrt{6}$ (negative values discarded)\\
Thus, the answer is: $CD=\boxed{\sqrt{6}}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\ it follows that $\angle ACD+\angle BCD=90^\circ$.\\ Since $CD$ is the altitude from the hypotenuse $AB$,\\ it follows that $\angle ADC=\angle CDB=90^\circ$, $\angle ACD+\angle CAD=90^\circ$,\\ therefore $\angle CAD=\angle BCD$,\\ therefore $\triangle CAD\sim \triangle BCD$,\\ therefore $\frac{AD}{CD}=\frac{CD}{BD}$,\\ therefore $CD^2=3\times 2=6$,\\ therefore $CD=\sqrt{6}$ (negative values discarded)\\ Thus, the answer is: $CD=\boxed{\sqrt{6}}$

Point C is above D, and line segment CD vertically connects C and D. A right angle is marked at D in the figure, indicating that CD is perpendicular to AB; there is also a right-angle mark at C, indicating that triangle ABC is right-angled at point C. No numerical lengths are directly marked in the figure; the problem statement gives AD=3, BD=2.

Reasoning: Because ∠ACB=90°, ∠ACD+∠BCD=90°. Also because CD is the altitude to hypotenuse AB, and A, D, B are collinear, ∠ADC=∠CDB=90°. In right triangle ACD, ∠ACD+∠CAD=90°, therefore ∠CAD=∠BCD. In this way, △CAD and △BCD have one equal right angle, and one pair of equal acute angles, so △CAD∼△BCD. From the corresponding side relationship of similar triangles, AD/CD = CD/BD can be obtained. Substituting AD=3, BD=2, gives CD^2=AD·BD=3×2=6. Since CD is a length, take the positive value, so CD=√6.
